title: Brush
why: Gaussian-splat trainer that runs on macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and in a browser over WebGPU, so a shop can train a product splat from its own photos without a CUDA box.

title: ooosplat
why: Desktop app that turns photos or video into a splat on Apple Silicon (Metal, alpha) with Brush and COLMAP bundled; exports PLY, compressed PLY, SPZ and SOG but no GLB, so a mesh step is still needed for a standard product viewer.

title: Modly
licence: MIT per README (GitHub index shows NOASSERTION)
why: Desktop app that turns one product photo into a 3D model on your own GPU (Windows, Linux, Apple Silicon, AMD via ROCm), with a CLI that writes GLB for the web.

title: AssetFurnace (image-to-3dlab)
licence: Apache-2.0 wrapper (wrapped models keep their own licences)
why: Local pipeline that wraps Pixal3D, TRELLIS.2, Hunyuan3D 2.1 and Stable Fast 3D behind one run, on Apple Silicon or NVIDIA Linux (24 GB VRAM tested), with GLB output.

title: TRELLIS
why: Single image to 3D asset (mesh, Gaussians or radiance field) with strong open quality, but it needs an NVIDIA GPU with 16 GB or more and was tested only on Linux, so it is a server job, not a Mac job.

title: Unique3D
why: Single image to textured mesh on one CUDA GPU (Ubuntu 22.04 with CUDA 12.1 in the README, plus a Windows installer), but the last push was July 2025, so expect dependency rot.

title: LichtFeld Studio
why: Native Gaussian-splat trainer and editor for NVIDIA CUDA 12.8+ that exports PLY, SOG, SPZ and a standalone HTML viewer, the richest export set in the bucket; GPL-3 means any modified copy you distribute must be shared.

title: spirula-studio
why: Video to splat to mesh with a Vulkan or CUDA backend, so it may run beyond NVIDIA; README not fetched, so check hardware and install before use.

title: OpenSfM
why: CPU structure-from-motion that turns a set of product photos into camera poses and a sparse point cloud, the cheap first stage before a dense or mesh step.

title: Meshroom
licence: MPL-2.0 per README (GitHub index shows NOASSERTION)
why: Node-based photogrammetry GUI (AliceVision) that turns photo sets into textured meshes; MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft, so your own site code stays yours; hardware was not checked in this sweep.

title: OpenDroneMap
why: Command-line photogrammetry that writes OBJ and PLY meshes on CPU by default (optional GPU SIFT image); built for drone imagery, so product turntables need tuning, and the AGPL network clause applies to modified copies served over a network.

title: Hunyuan3D 2.1
licence: Tencent Hunyuan Community Licence (excludes EU, UK and South Korea; separate licence above 1M MAU)
why: Image to PBR-textured 3D with strong material quality, but the licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea and caps MAU, so it is not free for a shop that may serve those markets; needs about 10 GB VRAM for shape and 21 GB for texture.

title: Free for Creators
licence: CC0-1.0 for the list; each linked asset carries its own licence
why: Licence-verified directory of free 3D sources (Poly Haven, ambientCG, Kenney, KayKit, NASA 3D as CC0, Poly Pizza per model) with attribution and monetisation rules per source, so you pick a model that is clear to use on a shop.

title: OS3A Gallery
licence: Not stated on repo; listed Polygonal Mind models are CC0 per README
why: Discovery site for CC0 GLB models (991+ in the Polygonal Mind collection per README), so a shop can find a ready-to-use GLB and read its licence in one place.

title: Retro3D Graphics Collection
licence: Not stated on repo; README says commercial use with no attribution or share-alike, assets CC0
why: Game-ready retro-style 3D assets that the README calls commercially usable with no attribution; textures must come from CC0 sources, so check each texture before use.

title: Objaverse-XL
why: 10M+ 3D object dataset with download scripts, but each object carries its own licence (many CC-BY or non-commercial), so filter per object before any use on a shop.

title: Matcaps
licence: None stated; source authors not traceable per README
why: Large matcap PNG library for stylised shading in three.js, but the licence is unclear and the sources are untraceable, so treat it as not cleared for a shop.

title: model-viewer
why: Web component that shows a GLB with orbit controls and AR on phones from one script tag or an npm install, the simplest product viewer for a shop page.

title: Online3DViewer
why: Browser viewer and converter for many 3D formats, useful for checking or converting a supplier's model before it goes on the site.

title: GaussianSplats3D
why: Three.js splat viewer for .ply, .splat and .ksplat, but the author says it is no longer actively developed and points to Spark, and it caps around 8 to 16M splats.

title: PlayCanvas model-viewer
why: One embeddable viewer for both glTF meshes and Gaussian splats, built on PlayCanvas and PCUI, so a shop can use a single component for either output.

title: supersplat-viewer
why: High-performance splat viewer with WebXR, the viewer behind superspl.at, for embedding a trained splat on a product page.

title: splat-transform
why: CLI and library that converts and compresses splats (PLY to compressed PLY or SOG), the step that makes a trained splat small enough for a product page.

title: spz
why: Niantic's SPZ splat format, about 10x smaller than PLY with little visible loss; LichtFeld and ooosplat both export it, so it is a shared target.

title: glTF-Transform
why: JavaScript SDK and CLI to optimise GLB files (mesh and texture compression, resizing), the cheapest way to shrink a generated model before it hits the page.

title: three.js
why: The base WebGL and WebGPU library under most viewers here, for any custom viewer a shop needs beyond the drop-in components.

title: Vanta.js
why: Animated 3D background effects for any page, about 120 KB min+gzip (mostly three.js); last push March 2024, so test it against your three.js version.

title: cobe
why: WebGL globe in about 5 KB with zero dependencies, a light way to show a shop's delivery area or origin on a page.

title: React Bits
why: Large set of animated React and Next.js components, free for personal and commercial use per README; the Pro tier is paid, and Commons Clause bars selling the library as a product, not using it on a shop.

title: canvas-ui
why: Canvas components with WebGL effects running over live HTML, for React, Vue, Svelte or vanilla; same Commons Clause limit as react-bits.

title: ThreeUI community edition
why: Login-free community edition of ThreeUI with live Three.js component pages and source; Pro and Beta components are removed, and the README carries a sponsor banner.

title: r3f-scroll-rig
why: Syncs react-three-fiber meshes to DOM elements on scroll, so a product model can move with the page; last push December 2025.

title: react-postprocessing
why: Post-processing effects for react-three-fiber scenes, only needed if the viewer must add effects such as bloom on top of the model.

title: drei
why: Helpers for react-three-fiber (controls, environment, GLTF loading), the usual base for a React product viewer scene.
